why_next: The frozen FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING verdict is valid but narrowly bounded: the failure is alpha=1.0 Laplace smoothing (88% pseudo-count mass, degenerate control K3=0.109 > stochastic K3=0.099) and sklearn discrete-mode k-invariance (k=5,10,20 all identical). Audit recomputes that MLE (alpha=0) K3=1.377 bits and alpha=0.1 K3=0.743 bits on the same N=5000 data — both exceed the 0.5 threshold. However, null centering for those alphas has NOT been measured (spec mandated alpha=1.0). The critical unknown is whether reduced smoothing preserves |shuffled null_mean| < 0.1 while recovering sensitivity. This directly resolves whether the CMI pathway is blocked by hyperparameter choice (fixable) or by discrete state-space structure (fundamental). If alpha=0.1 achieves both C1 and C3, the pathway is unblocked and beyond-Markov K3-K2 testing can proceed. If null centering degrades, the combination of sensitivity and false-positive control may be fundamentally constrained on discrete 12-state data.

established: Null centering (C1) is robust across all estimator families on stochastic 12-state SPA at N=5000 with within-session shuffle: plug-in KL |null_mean|=0.064, KSG k=5/10/20 |null_mean|=0.012, all < 0.1 threshold with 1.6-8x margin. (EXP-PHYSICS-35510154353 result.json:controls.C1-NULL-CONTROL pass=true, 4/4 estimators)

sklearn.feature_selection.mutual_info_classif with discrete_features=True is k-invariant on purely discrete data: K3=0.000560, mi_joint=0.034413, mi_cond=0.033853 identical for k=5, k=10, k=20. Implementation uses categorical exact matching, not distance-based neighborhoods. (EXP-PHYSICS-35510154353 result.json:metrics.ksg_k_invariance; audit.json V3-KSG_discrete_k_invariance)

Plug-in KL with alpha=1.0 Laplace smoothing has bias exceeding the true signal: degenerate control K3=0.109 on deterministic SPA (I=0) > stochastic K3=0.099 (I=1.52 bits). 88% of probability mass is pseudo-counts (n_smoothed=45368 from N=5000 data). Smoothing alone determines outcome. (EXP-PHYSICS-35510154353 result.json:metrics.plugin_kl_smoothing_bias; audit.json V2-plug_in_KL_Laplace_smoothing_bias)

True I(Y;A|Z) on stochastic 12-state SPA is 1.52 bits (audit-confirmed from parent EXP-PHYSICS-35482477045 via exact enumeration and N=50000 empirical plug-in). Per-stratum PMI 1.46-1.69 bits across 48/48 strata (all p=0.0 after Bonferroni) confirms signal is strong and detectable by non-parametric tests. (EXP-PHYSICS-35510154353 result.json:metrics.permutation_test_exploratory; parent audit.json V1-theoretical_CMI_miscalibrated)
KSG CMI k=5 replication exactly matches parent: K3=0.000560 (0.007% error from parent 0.000560). Reproducibility confirmed. (EXP-PHYSICS-35510154353 result.json:controls.REPLICATION-B-PARENT-KSG-K5)

Audit MLE recomputation on same N=5000 records: alpha=0 (MLE) K3=1.377, alpha=0.1 K3=0.743, alpha=0.01 K3=1.274, alpha=0.001 K3=1.366 — all exceed 0.5 threshold. At N=50000: MLE K3=1.447. The signal IS recoverable with reduced smoothing. (audit.json:recomputed_metrics.plugin_KL_alpha_sensitivity_recompute_N5000_K3)

do_not_assume: The frozen FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING verdict closes the C-WEB-DYNAMICS claim or the Physics lane. It closes only the plug-in KL alpha=1.0 and sklearn discrete KSG k=10 pathways on this specific SPA class. Alternative estimators and hyperparameters remain untested.

CMI estimation is fundamentally impossible on discrete SPAs. The audit demonstrates MLE alpha=0 recovers K3=1.377 bits on the same data — the signal is detectable with unbiased estimation. The failure is hyperparameter-specific.

The 1.52-bit true CMI is undetectable in principle. Per-stratum PMI 1.46-1.69 bits across all 48 strata (p=0.0) and MLE 1.377 bits confirm the signal is strong and detectable by appropriate estimators.

KSG CMI family is universally k-invariant. The invariance is specific to sklearn.feature_selection.mutual_info_classif with discrete_features=True on categorical data. Continuous KSG or alternative implementations may behave differently.
Alpha=1.0 is the only valid Laplace smoothing choice. The audit shows alpha=0.1 gives K3=0.743 (would pass C3), suggesting smaller alpha is viable — pending null centering verification.

Production Web transitions generalize from this synthetic 12-state SPA. The SPA has hash routing, 4 candidates per (state,action), no anti-bot, auth, visual complexity, or stochastic production dynamics.
The within-session shuffle correction changes C1 pass/fail. C1 margin is 1.6-8x below threshold for plug-in KL and 8x for KSG; correction does not affect outcome.

recommended_action: Design a new frozen experiment testing plug-in KL with an alpha sweep (alpha=0 MLE, 0.01, 0.1, 0.5, 1.0) on the same stochastic SPA at N=5000. For EACH alpha, measure both C1 (500 within-session shuffled-action permutations) and C3 (positive control vs 0.5 threshold). This resolves the critical unknown: whether reduced smoothing preserves null centering while recovering sensitivity. If alpha=0.1 achieves C1+C3 (|null_mean|<0.1 AND K3>=0.5), the CMI pathway is unblocked and the next experiment should test beyond-Markov K3-K2. If null centering degrades monotonically with alpha, the sensitivity-false-positive tradeoff is characterized and the Physics lane can make an informed pivot decision. Do NOT repeat the frozen alpha=1.0 configuration.
